evidence: Mechanism confirmed in the frozen tree. process_inbox_pr_review's locked recheck is strict greater-than (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1189-1197), and _upsert_pull_request refreshes on payload_updated_at__lte (tasks.py:349-358), so with equal clocks pr_obj.payload_updated_at == incoming and the recheck passes. The dedupe lookup keys on head_sha=H1 only (tasks.py:1201-1208), so a live H2 run is invisible to it, and _supersede_prior_runs (tasks.py:415-433, called at 1218) supersedes every non-terminal run for the PR with no head comparison. The H1 run then hits post_verdict's live-head guard (temporal/activities.py:672-686): it marks itself SUPERSEDED and returns skipped_head_moved; nothing re-queues H2 (no handling of that outcome in temporal/workflow.py, and tasks/schedules.py only carries the digest beat). Existing tests cover strictly-older snapshots only (tests/test_tasks.py:1024-1048, 454-480). Reachability is narrow: GitHub updated_at is second-granular, so it needs the H1-bearing update and the H2 push in the same wall-clock second, the REST fetch returning H1 (pre-push or lagging replica), and the H2 synchronize (routed through _inbox_rereview_carve_out, tasks.py:144-216) committing before the inbox transaction that opens immediately after the fetch (tasks.py:1160-1187). The webhook path has the identical strict-> semantics by design ('Equal timestamps proceed (a redelivery of the current head)', tasks.py:1010-1014, locked recheck 1036-1046), so two same-second synchronize deliveries out of order already carry the same exposure; the inbox leg mirrors it rather than introducing it. Consequence is fail-safe: no approval is posted for the wrong head, H2 just goes unreviewed until the next receiver refire (review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-140 fires on every TaskRun output save carrying pr_url; the refire dedupes on the current head and creates the missing run, tasks.py:1198-1216, test_tasks.py:992-1021 'missed_webhook_head_gets_reviewed') or the next push.
notes: Would drop to not-real if GitHub guaranteed distinct updated_at per head-changing event (it does not; second precision). Would rise to should_fix if same-second pushes are common in the self-driving agent flow, or if a missed draft-time verdict blocks Inbox triage with no later output save to refire the receiver. A narrower fix than the suggestion also works: on an equal clock, skip supersede when a non-terminal run exists at a different head, or compare the live head inside the transaction; the webhook path's equal-clock semantics would need the same treatment for consistency.
